---
title: "Worklist regulatory gates"
---

`PackedRegulatoryRules`, `PackedRegulatoryState`, and
`cuda::evaluate_regulatory_gates` implement caller-authored boolean eligibility
programs. The rule bank is shared; input and accessibility bits are private to
each instance. The CUDA kernel evaluates only an explicit list of
`(instance, rule)` occurrences. It does not construct a dense gene-by-module
matrix or infer a biological ontology from bit positions.

For an occurrence with instance state `x`, rule `r` is eligible exactly when:

```text
accessible(instance, r)
    AND every required input bit of r is active in x
    AND no forbidden input bit of r is active in x
```

Empty required/forbidden sets form a true conjunction; accessibility still
applies. Repeated worklist occurrences remain distinct output occurrences.
This is the same conjunction/open-flag semantics as the native
`AccessibilityState` class. These programs are model gates, not a claim that
the caller's biological rules are correct.

## Shared structure and private state

`PackedRegulatoryRules` takes explicit stable rule IDs and required/forbidden
input **bit positions**. It sorts rules by stable ID, rejects duplicate IDs,
out-of-domain bits, duplicate inputs and required/forbidden contradictions, and
stores sparse `(word, required_mask, forbidden_mask)` records. CSR offsets give
each rule's touched words. A rule that mentions two words occupies two mask
records regardless of the full input domain size.

`rule_ordinal(id)` resolves a stable ID to its dense bank position. The
`structure_epoch()` and caller's input-ID-to-bit map identify the projection.
The borrowed device view does not check or preserve external metadata: retain
the bank, its epoch, and the exact identity map for the lifetime of device
execution. Changing the rule bank requires rebuilding its projection and
updating dependent worklists. Never cast an entity ID or rule ID directly to a
dense bit/ordinal.

`PackedRegulatoryState` owns input words and accessibility words for one
instance. A C++ copy explicitly inherits the current bits and subsequent
mutations are independent. `set_input(bit, value)` changes an input;
`set_accessible(rule_ordinal, value)` changes permission to evaluate a rule.
The CUDA state view lays multiple instances out with explicit word strides,
which may include padding. Tail input bits beyond the declared domain cannot
be referenced by a rule.

Accessibility is a modeled permission. It does not mean that a physical cache
line, parameter block or numerical output is resident or valid. Physical
placement and the [incremental cache](incremental_cellular.qmd) retain their
separate ownership and invalidation contracts.

## Converting inherited native accessibility

The caller retains its original `AccessibilityProgram<Id>` definitions and
an ordered `input_ids` mapping. Translate `required_inputs` and
`forbidden_inputs` through that mapping to populate `RegulatoryRule` bit
positions. Native program IDs must have an explicit reversible encoding if
they are not already `uint64_t`; this CUDA-facing bank does not invent one.

The following conversion reads an inherited native state without changing it:

```cpp
// bank contains the translated programs; input_ids is the exact bit mapping.
// inherited is an AccessibilityState<uint64_t>, possibly returned by fork().
cellerator::modeling::cuda::PackedRegulatoryState packed(
    input_ids.size(), bank.rule_ids().size(), false);
for (std::size_t bit = 0; bit < input_ids.size(); ++bit)
    packed.set_input(bit, inherited.input_active(input_ids[bit]));
for (std::size_t rule = 0; rule < bank.rule_ids().size(); ++rule)
    packed.set_accessible(rule, inherited.is_open(bank.rule_ids()[rule]));
```

Record the native structure revision, program revisions, state generation,
bank structure epoch and input mapping alongside the uploaded projection.
Provenance and copy-on-write ancestry remain with the native owner; uploading
packed words does not transfer or automatically synchronize that history.
An external threshold or hysteresis policy may update native accessibility,
but no numeric threshold or approximation is built into this boolean kernel.

## Sparse execution and outputs

Construct `RegulatoryOccurrence` entries from the caller's active worklist.
The changed-source [frontier primitive](incremental_cellular.qmd#cuda-changed-source-frontier)
provides invalidated interaction ordinals; map those through the retained
interaction-to-rule mapping and the affected instance identity. These are
different identity spaces and are not assumed to share dense ordinals.

Upload the bank's offsets/masks and each instance's input/accessibility words,
then call `evaluate_regulatory_gates` with the borrowed views, explicit stream,
worklist and output storage. The function performs no allocation, implicit
synchronization, device switch, dependency discovery, or host status copy.
Callers retain all buffers through stream completion and prevent overlapping
mutations of inputs or outputs. The function evaluates the supplied input
snapshot; it does not update state or numerical interaction caches.

Output eligibility is packed by **worklist occurrence position**, not by a
dense instance-by-rule matrix. For occurrence `i`, inspect bit `i % 64` of
output word `i / 64`. Unused bits of the final output word are zeroed. Optional
compaction returns eligible occurrence indices; use each index to recover its
original instance and rule. Compaction order is unspecified. It preserves
duplicate occurrences and does not deduplicate their downstream contributions.

The synchronous CUDA return reports argument/launch errors. After completion,
`RegulatoryGateStatus` reports device-content errors and bounded compaction
overflow. On any status flag, neither output is publishable; storage can have
partial writes and `compact_written` is zero. Overflow alone retains the exact
`eligible_count`, allowing a retry with sufficient capacity. Without compaction,
`eligible_count` is still reported and `compact_written` remains zero.
Caller-supplied pointer extents and non-aliasing remain caller obligations;
the kernel checks selected instance/rule indices, CSR ranges, word indices,
overlapping required/forbidden masks and referenced tail bits.

The execution cost is output-bit initialization plus the sum of touched rule
words over supplied occurrences. The representation uses shared sparse rule
masks and private packed bitsets; it does not promise faster execution than
another implementation. Preparation, upload, worklist construction, output
consumption and synchronization belong in a complete-path measurement.

## Validation boundary

The [smoke fixture](../tests/framework/cuda/regulatory_gates_smoke.cu) compiled
and linked with CUDA 12.9 for `sm_70`. Its `--host-only` path was executed and
passed; that branch returns before device discovery, allocation or kernel
launch. An independent scalar boolean oracle
matched the packed representation over 70 occurrences, including required and
forbidden bits crossing input word boundaries, accessibility beyond rule 63,
empty conjunctions, duplicate occurrences and independently mutated inherited
state. Host construction also checks malformed rules.

```sh
nvcc -std=c++17 -arch=sm_70 -Iinclude \
  tests/framework/cuda/regulatory_gates_smoke.cu \
  src/modeling/cuda/regulatory_gates.cu \
  -o /tmp/cellerator-regulatory-gates-smoke
/tmp/cellerator-regulatory-gates-smoke --host-only
```

The fixture's device path additionally checks packed output against that
oracle, compaction, capacity overflow, guard words, invalid occurrences and
malformed sparse masks. These occurrence-based device cases passed on V100;
the suite-wide sanitizer outcomes and test limits are in the
[validation report](../planning/v100-framework-2026-10-29/REPORT.md). Performance
and biological validity remain unestablished. GPU execution continues to
require the repository's admitted execution route. The optional CMake smoke
target is build-only and is not
registered as an automatically executed CTest.

## Experimental independent-cell bitplanes

`evaluate_regulatory_bitplanes` is a separate experimental entrypoint. A
`uint32_t` stores one bit for each of 32 independent cells; feature planes use
`features[feature * instance_word_count + instance_word]`. Shared rules contain
sparse required/forbidden **feature indices**, with separate CSR offsets.
The caller supplies `(rule, instance_word)` work items and a validity mask for
every instance word, including its tail. Optional accessibility planes use
`accessibility[rule * instance_word_count + instance_word]`; a null pointer
explicitly means all cells are accessible.

For each work item, the kernel starts with validity/accessibility and applies
AND for each required feature plane and ANDNOT for each forbidden plane. It
returns one packed eligibility word per item. Empty conjunctions return the
valid accessible cells. The output can feed subsequent Boolean transitions
without extracting cells; separate buffers are required for input and next
state. Duplicate work items remain duplicate words. No compaction, conversion,
representation selection or numerical approximation is implicit.

The design is an experimental **probe**, alongside the arbitrary-occurrence
implementation. KernelBender's
`references/bridges/bitplanes.md` (recognition, construction and first
discriminator) motivates keeping independent Boolean states in word bits;
`references/compositions/discrete-state.md` (construction and representation
and lifetime) motivates retaining planes across transitions. These references
were read from
`/home/tumlinson/kda/skills/KernelBender/skills/kernelbender/`.
They also warn that conversion, extraction, tails and changed routing can
dominate. This entrypoint does not implement carry-save counts, thresholds or
cross-word neighboring-cell transitions.

The CPU fixture exhausts three-feature truth assignments distributed over
32 cells, checks a second word with nine valid tail cells against scalar gates,
and consumes the resulting plane in a second Boolean transition. Focused V100
device checks for the bitplane kernel are summarized in the
[validation report](../planning/v100-framework-2026-10-29/REPORT.md). No
performance advantage or automatic dispatch preference is established. A
future decision requires comparing both representations over identical work,
including cold conversion, state updates, repeated transitions, extraction and
compaction.
